recipes.title: Tall Buttermilk Ricotta Pancakes
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Ricotta-rich pancakes that rise tall and stay tender for hours.
recipes.lede: I stopped chasing fluffy pancakes the day I started folding ricotta into the batter. The cheese holds moisture the way buttermilk alone never could, so these stay custardy in the middle even after the third batch has come off the griddle. Lemon zest is not optional in my kitchen - it keeps a stack this rich from tasting heavy.

steps.title: Whisk the dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a wide bowl until no streaks of soda remain. Doing this properly is the difference between an even rise and a pancake with bitter pockets.

steps.title: Build the wet
steps.text: In a second bowl whisk the buttermilk, ricotta, egg yolks, melted butter, vanilla and lemon zest until the ricotta breaks down into fine curds and the mixture pours in a smooth ribbon.

steps.title: Whip the whites
steps.text: Beat the egg whites with a hand mixer until they hold a soft peak that flops over at the tip - about 90 seconds. Stop before they look dry and grainy or they will fold in as lumps.

steps.title: Fold, then rest
steps.text: Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until the last dry patch disappears, then fold in the whites in two additions. The batter should be thick enough to mound on a spoon. Let it sit 10 minutes while the griddle heats.

steps.title: Griddle low and slow
steps.text: Heat a griddle or heavy skillet over medium-low and wipe with oil. Ladle scant 1/3-cup pools and cook until the edges look matte and bubbles open and stay open in the center, 3 to 4 minutes.

steps.title: Flip once
steps.text: Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the second side is deep gold and the pancake springs back when pressed at the center. Hold finished pancakes in a single layer on a rack in a 200F/95C oven - stacking them steams the crust soft.

tips: Medium-low is the whole trick. On high heat the outside sets before the ricotta-heavy middle cooks, and you get a raw seam.
No buttermilk? Stir 1 1/2 tablespoons lemon juice into 1 1/2 cups whole milk and let it sit 10 minutes.
The batter keeps covered in the fridge for 2 days. It loses a little lift, so add an extra 1/4 teaspoon baking powder on day two.
recipes.cooksNote: A rack, not a plate. I lost years of good pancakes to the well-meaning habit of stacking them on a warm plate, where trapped steam turns that hard-won crisp edge into a damp one. Spread them on a wire rack in a low oven and the last pancake off the griddle eats exactly like the first.

recipes.title: Red Pepper Shakshuka with Feta
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Eggs poached in a slow-cooked pepper and tomato sauce, finished with feta.
recipes.lede: Shakshuka lives or dies on how long you cook the peppers, and most recipes rush them. Give the onion and pepper a full fifteen minutes to collapse and sweeten and you get a sauce with real depth instead of one that tastes like warm canned tomato. Toasting the spices in the oil first is the second half of the job.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.text: Warm the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and peppers with a good pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, until they are limp, glossy and starting to catch gold at the edges, 14 to 16 minutes.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Push the vegetables to one side, add the garlic, paprika, cumin and caraway to the bare oil and stir for 45 seconds, until the spices smell toasty and the garlic is fragrant but not browned. Stir in the harissa.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes with their juice and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Simmer briskly, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick enough that a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a track that fills in slowly, 12 to 15 minutes.

steps.title: Make the wells
steps.text: Taste and adjust the salt now - you cannot season it properly once the eggs are in. Use the back of a spoon to hollow out six wells, spacing them around the pan, and crack an egg into each.

steps.title: Poach covered
steps.text: Cover, lower the heat and cook 6 to 9 minutes. Pull the pan the moment the whites are opaque all the way to the yolk and the yolks still wobble when you shake the handle. They set fast on carryover heat.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter the feta and cilantro over the top, drizzle with a little more olive oil and bring the pan to the table with warm flatbread for scooping.

tips: Hand-crushed whole tomatoes beat pre-crushed every time - you get real pieces of fruit in the sauce instead of a uniform puree.
Crack each egg into a small cup first, then tip it into its well. It keeps the yolks whole and the wells tidy.
For a milder pan, halve the harissa and add a teaspoon of honey with the tomatoes.
recipes.cooksNote: This is a sauce recipe with eggs in it, so make the sauce ahead if you like. It keeps five days in the fridge and improves on day two once the caraway settles in. Reheat until it bubbles at the edges before you make the wells, or the eggs will sit in lukewarm sauce and take forever to set.

recipes.title: Maple Pecan Overnight Oats
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Thick, creamy jars with toasted pecans and real maple - five minutes tonight.
recipes.lede: Most overnight oats end up as cold porridge soup because the ratio is wrong and nothing in the jar has any texture. Two tablespoons of chia thicken this to a spoon-standing set, and the pecans go in toasted and stay on top until morning. I make four jars on Sunday and the week gets noticeably easier.

items.name: Pure maple syrup
items.note: grade A dark if you have it

steps.title: Toast the pecans
steps.text: Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat, tossing often, until they smell nutty and a broken one shows a pale tan interior, 4 to 5 minutes. Tip them onto a plate right away - the pan will keep cooking them.

steps.title: Mix the base
steps.text: In a large bowl whisk the milk, yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon and fine salt until completely smooth with no yogurt lumps clinging to the whisk.

steps.title: Add the grains
steps.text: Stir in the oats, chia and mashed banana. Keep stirring for a full 30 seconds - chia clumps the instant it hits liquid and those clumps never soften.

steps.title: Jar it up
steps.text: Divide among four 8-ounce jars, tapping each on the counter to settle out air pockets, and leave about half an inch of headroom. Seal and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Check the set
steps.text: In the morning the oats should hold a spoon-shaped hollow that fills in slowly. If it is looser than you like, stir in another teaspoon of chia and give it 20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and eat
steps.text: Top each jar with chopped dates, the toasted pecans and a few flakes of salt just before eating so the nuts stay crisp.

tips: Rolled oats only. Quick oats dissolve into paste by morning and steel-cut never soften at all.
The jars keep 4 days. Hold the nuts and dates separately in a small container and top at the last second.
Swap the milk for full-fat coconut and the yogurt for coconut yogurt to make it dairy-free without losing the body.
recipes.cooksNote: Sweetness is personal and this is deliberately at the low end - three tablespoons of maple across four jars. Taste the base before you divide it, while you can still fix it. Once the oats hydrate, stirring in more syrup thins the whole thing back out and you are chasing the texture again.

recipes.title: Brown Butter Banana Bread
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Deep, nutty and properly moist, with a crackly turbinado top.
recipes.lede: Browning the butter takes six extra minutes and changes the loaf completely - it adds a toasted, almost butterscotch note that plain melted butter cannot touch. Dark brown sugar and a spoonful of yogurt do the rest. This is the loaf my kids ask for by name, and it slices clean even while it is still slightly warm.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat, swirling, until the foam subsides and the milk solids at the bottom turn the color of dark honey and smell like toasted nuts, 5 to 7 minutes. Scrape every brown speck into a large bowl and cool 10 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350F/175C. Butter a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan and line it with a parchment sling that overhangs the long sides - this loaf is tender and you will want the handles.

steps.title: Whisk the dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon together in a separate bowl until evenly combined and no lumps of soda remain.

steps.title: Build the batter
steps.text: Whisk the brown sugar into the cooled butter, then the eggs one at a time, then the yogurt and vanilla. Mash the bananas until only a few small lumps remain and stir them in. The mixture should look glossy and slack.

steps.title: Fold, do not beat
steps.text: Add the dry ingredients and the walnuts and fold with a spatula just until the last dry streak vanishes - about 15 strokes. Overmixing here is what makes banana bread gummy and tight.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scrape into the pan, smooth the top and scatter over the turbinado sugar. Bake 55 to 65 minutes, until the top is domed and split, a skewer in the center comes out with moist crumbs but no wet batter, and the internal temperature reads 205F/96C.

steps.title: Cool properly
steps.text: Cool in the pan 20 minutes, then lift out by the sling and cool on a rack at least another 30 minutes. Cutting a hot loaf compresses the crumb into a dense stripe down the middle.

tips: Bananas should be more black than yellow. If yours are only just ripe, roast them in their skins at 350F/175C for 15 minutes and cool before mashing.
The loaf freezes beautifully. Wrap cooled slices individually and they toast straight from frozen.
Skip the walnuts and fold in 3/4 cup dark chocolate chunks instead - the brown butter takes to chocolate very well.
Do not use a dark nonstick pan without dropping the oven to 335F/168C, or the sides will be leathery before the middle sets.
recipes.cooksNote: Weigh the flour if you own a scale. Banana bread has enough moisture in it to hide a lot of sins, but an extra 30 grams of scooped flour is the single most common reason a loaf comes out dry and crumbly rather than dense and damp. If you are measuring by cup, fluff the flour first, spoon it in and level with a knife.

recipes.title: Rosemary Sourdough Focaccia
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: An open, olive-oil-crisped slab with a long cold ferment and no kneading.
recipes.lede: This is the loaf that made me stop buying bread. The dough is stirred together with a spoon, folded four times over two hours and then left in the fridge overnight, which is where all the flavour actually comes from. What comes out is a shatter-crisp bottom, a custardy middle and a top full of dimples holding pools of green olive oil.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Whisk the starter, water and honey in a large bowl until the starter dissolves and the water looks cloudy. Add the flour and salt and stir with a sturdy spoon until no dry flour remains - it will be a shaggy, sticky mass. Cover and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Fold four times
steps.text: With a wet hand, reach under one side of the dough, stretch it up and fold it over the center; rotate the bowl and repeat three more times. Do this whole set every 30 minutes for 2 hours. By the last set the dough should feel smooth, elastic and noticeably puffed.

steps.title: Cold ferment
steps.text: Cover tightly and refrigerate 12 to 16 hours. The dough should rise by roughly half and be dotted with bubbles across the surface when you pull it out - this slow cold stretch is where the sour, wheaty flavour develops.

steps.title: Pan and warm up
steps.text: Pour 3 tablespoons of the olive oil into a 13-by-9-inch metal pan and tilt to coat. Scrape in the dough, turn it once to oil both sides, and let it sit at room temperature 2 to 3 hours until it relaxes to fill most of the pan and jiggles like set custard.

steps.title: Dimple and top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450F/230C. Oil your fingertips and press straight down through the dough to the pan bottom all over, making deep dimples. Drizzle with the remaining oil, then scatter the rosemary, garlic, flaky salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bake hot
steps.text: Bake 22 to 28 minutes, until the top is deep golden brown, the edges have pulled from the pan and shrunk slightly, and the underside is crisp when you lift a corner with a spatula.

steps.title: Slide out immediately
steps.text: Slide the focaccia straight onto a wire rack the moment it leaves the oven. Leaving it in the hot pan steams that crisp bottom soft within minutes. Cool 15 minutes before cutting.

tips: Your starter must be at its peak - domed and bubbly, not collapsed. A sluggish starter gives a dense, flat slab no amount of extra time will fix.
Metal pan, not glass. Glass insulates and you will never get the fried, crisp underside that makes this worth doing.
Leftovers split horizontally and grilled make the best sandwich bread in this house.
recipes.cooksNote: The half cup of olive oil looks alarming and it is not a mistake. The oil in the pan effectively shallow-fries the base while the top bakes, and that contrast between crackling bottom and open, tender crumb is the entire point of pan focaccia. Use oil you would happily taste on a salad, because you will absolutely taste it here.

recipes.title: Overnight Cardamom Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Soft cardamom-scented rolls shaped the night before, baked straight from the fridge.
recipes.lede: Nobody wants to make enriched dough at six in the morning, so this one does all its work overnight in the fridge. Cardamom in the dough is the Scandinavian move that keeps a pan of cinnamon rolls from tasting one-note sweet. They come out pull-apart soft in the middle with caramelised edges, and the tangy cream cheese glaze goes on while they are still warm.

steps.title: Start the dough
steps.text: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and let stand 5 minutes, until the surface is foamy. In a stand mixer with the dough hook, add the flour, salt, cardamom, eggs and the milk mixture and mix on low until a rough dough forms, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add butter and knead
steps.text: With the mixer on medium-low, add the softened butter a piece at a time, waiting for each to disappear. Knead 8 to 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, pulls cleanly from the bowl sides and stretches into a thin translucent sheet without tearing.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise at room temperature until doubled and a floured fingertip pressed into it leaves a dent that fills back only halfway, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Mash the filling butter, brown sugar and cinnamon into a paste. Roll the dough on a lightly floured counter into an 18-by-14-inch rectangle, spread the paste to within half an inch of the far long edge, then roll up snugly from the near long edge.

steps.title: Cut and chill
steps.text: Trim the ends and cut 12 equal rolls with unflavored dental floss or a very sharp knife. Arrange cut side up in a buttered 13-by-9-inch pan with a little space between, cover tightly and refrigerate 8 to 12 hours.

steps.title: Warm and bake
steps.text: Take the pan out and let it sit at room temperature 45 to 60 minutes, until the rolls look puffy and have grown into each other. Heat the oven to 350F/175C and bake 28 to 33 minutes, until deep golden and the center roll reads 190F/88C.

steps.title: Glaze warm
steps.text: Beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar and lemon juice until smooth and pourable, adding a splash of milk if needed. Spread over the rolls after 10 minutes of cooling - hot rolls melt the glaze to nothing, cold ones will not take it.

tips: Grind whole green cardamom pods yourself if you can. Pre-ground loses most of its perfume within a few months.
Dental floss makes far cleaner cuts than a knife - slide it under the log, cross the ends over the top and pull.
Underbake by two minutes rather than over. The center roll is the last to finish and the first to dry out.
For gooier rolls, pour 1/4 cup warm heavy cream over the pan just before it goes into the oven.
recipes.cooksNote: The overnight chill is doing two jobs, not one. It buys you a civilised morning, but it also slows fermentation enough that the flavour deepens well past what a same-day dough can manage. If you are short on time you can rise, shape and bake in one stretch - just give the shaped rolls a full hour at room temperature and expect a slightly plainer, sweeter roll.

recipes.title: Freezer-Friendly Breakfast Burritos
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Crisp potatoes, soft-scrambled eggs and chorizo, rolled tight and griddled.
recipes.lede: The reason most homemade breakfast burritos turn soggy is wet eggs, so these get scrambled deliberately underdone and cooled before rolling. Everything else is about texture: potatoes roasted until the edges shatter, chorizo rendered properly, and a hard sear on the seam so the whole thing holds together in one hand. Six go in the freezer and breakfast is solved for a week.

steps.title: Roast the potatoes
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F/220C. Toss the diced potato with the olive oil, smoked paprika and a teaspoon of salt, spread on a sheet pan in a single layer and roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once, until deeply browned and crisp at the corners.

steps.title: Render the chorizo
steps.text: Meanwhile cook the chorizo in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until the fat has rendered out and the meat is browned in spots and no longer pink, 8 to 10 minutes. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.

steps.title: Soft-scramble the eggs
steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the milk and a good pinch of salt. Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low and add the eggs, stirring slowly and constantly. Pull them off the heat while they still look glossy and slightly underdone - they will set as they cool.

steps.title: Cool everything
steps.text: Spread the eggs, chorizo and potatoes on a sheet pan and let them cool to just barely warm, about 10 minutes. Rolling hot filling steams the tortilla from the inside and guarantees a soggy burrito.

steps.title: Roll them tight
steps.text: Warm the tortillas briefly so they flex. Lay a sixth of the cheese, potatoes, chorizo, eggs, salsa and scallions in a log slightly below center. Fold in the sides, then roll up firmly, tucking the filling back with your fingers as you go.

steps.title: Sear the seam
steps.text: Set a dry skillet over medium heat and place each burrito seam side down. Press gently and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until the tortilla is spotted golden and rigid enough to hold its shape when you pick it up.

tips: Drain the salsa in a sieve first. Wet salsa is the number one cause of a burrito that falls apart at the second bite.
To freeze, cool completely, wrap each in foil, then bag. They keep 3 months.
Reheat from frozen: unwrap, microwave 2 minutes on 50 percent power, then crisp both sides in a dry skillet for 3 minutes.
recipes.cooksNote: Ten-inch tortillas are the minimum here. Smaller ones tear on the fold and you end up compensating by underfilling, which gives you a thin, bready burrito. If your tortillas have been in the fridge, twenty seconds a side in a dry pan makes them pliable again - a cold tortilla will crack straight down the fold every time.

recipes.title: Blueberry Lemon Cream Scones
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Craggy, tender scones made with frozen grated butter and heavy cream.
recipes.lede: Grating frozen butter on a box grater is the one technique that turned my scones around - you get shards rather than pebbles, and those shards steam into flaky layers. Cream instead of milk keeps the crumb rich without making it heavy. They take about twenty minutes of hands-on work and taste like a very good bakery.

steps.title: Prep and chill
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400F/205C and line a sheet pan with parchment. Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl, then rub in the lemon zest with your fingertips until the mixture smells sharply of lemon.

steps.title: Grate the butter
steps.text: Grate the frozen butter on the large holes of a box grater directly into the flour, tossing every so often so the shreds stay separate. Toss until every piece is coated and the mixture looks like coarse, floury snow.

steps.title: Mix the liquid
steps.text: Whisk 3/4 cup of the cream with the egg and vanilla. Pour it over the flour mixture and stir with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms with dry patches still visible - fewer than 20 strokes.

steps.title: Fold in the berries
steps.text: Add the blueberries and fold two or three times only. The dough will look underhydrated and messy; that is correct, and squeezing it smooth here is what gives you flat, tough scones.

steps.title: Shape and cut
steps.text: Turn out onto a floured counter, pat into a 7-inch round about 1 1/4 inches thick, and cut into 8 wedges with a sharp knife pressed straight down - do not saw or twist, which seals the edges shut.

steps.title: Chill, then bake
steps.text: Space the wedges on the sheet pan and freeze 15 minutes. Brush the tops with the remaining cream, sprinkle heavily with turbinado, and bake 20 to 24 minutes, until risen tall, golden brown on top and firm at the base when tapped.

steps.title: Cool briefly
steps.text: Cool on the pan 5 minutes so the crumb sets, then move to a rack. They are best within a few hours of baking, still faintly warm.

tips: The 15-minute freeze before baking is what makes them rise straight up instead of spreading. Do not skip it.
Frozen blueberries work but do not thaw them, and expect a little purple streaking in the dough.
Unbaked wedges freeze for 2 months. Bake straight from the freezer and add 4 to 5 minutes.
recipes.cooksNote: Every step of this recipe is really about keeping the butter cold. Those grated shards need to reach the oven still solid so they burst into steam and push the layers apart - if the dough turns soft and greasy while you are shaping, stop and put the whole bowl in the freezer for ten minutes. Warm scone dough bakes into something closer to a sweet biscuit than a scone.

recipes.title: Thai Congee
recipes.author: Jet Tila
recipes.desc: Silky rice porridge with springy pork meatballs, ginger, and a jammy soft-boiled egg on top.
recipes.lede: This is the bowl I make when someone in the house is under the weather, and also the bowl I make when nobody is. Congee asks for one cup of rice and a lot of patience, and it pays you back with something that tastes far richer than its ingredient list. The pork meatballs are what turn it from a sickbed remedy into an actual dinner.

items.name: jasmine rice
items.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

items.name: fresh ginger
items.note: finely julienned, plus more for serving

steps.title: Start the porridge
steps.text: Combine the rinsed rice, stock, and half the ginger in a heavy pot and bring to a boil over high heat. Drop to a bare simmer, set the lid ajar, and cook for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes so the bottom does not catch.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.text: While the rice cooks, work the ground pork together with the garlic, fish sauce, white pepper, and cornstarch until the mixture turns slightly sticky and holds together when you press it. Chill until you need it.

steps.title: Check the texture
steps.text: The congee is ready when the grains have burst open and the whole pot moves like loose oatmeal, coating a spoon but still sliding off it. If it is too thick, loosen with hot stock a half cup at a time.

steps.title: Poach the meatballs
steps.text: Pinch off teaspoon-sized pieces of pork and drop them straight into the simmering congee. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until they float and are firm and opaque all the way through when you cut one open.

steps.title: Soft-boil the eggs
steps.text: Lower the eggs into a separate pot of boiling water and cook exactly 6 minutes, then move them to ice water for 2 minutes before peeling. The white should be set and the yolk still liquid at the center.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Salt the congee to taste — it needs more than you think. Ladle into deep bowls, halve an egg over each, and finish with the remaining ginger, scallions, cilantro, garlic oil, and a drizzle of soy.

tips: Rinse the rice properly. Cloudy water in the pot means gummy congee later.
A wooden spoon scraped across the bottom every ten minutes is the whole technique.
Leftovers set up like concrete in the fridge — reheat with an extra cup of stock and it comes right back.
recipes.cooksNote: The eggs are the part people get wrong. Six minutes in hard-boiling water gives a fully set white with a molten center; five minutes gives you a softer, saucier yolk that runs into the congee, and I go closer to five when the eggs are straight from the fridge and closer to six when they are at room temperature. Either way, straight into ice water afterward or they keep cooking in the shell.

recipes.title: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Beef short ribs braised in red wine until the meat slumps off the bone into its own glossy sauce.
recipes.lede: There is no way to make this fast and there is no reason to want to. Three hours in a low oven turns tough, marbled short rib into something you can serve with a spoon, and the wine reduces down into a sauce that tastes like it took a professional kitchen to make. Make it the day before if you can — it is genuinely better on day two.

steps.title: Season and dredge
steps.text: Salt and pepper the short ribs on all sides, then dust them lightly with flour and shake off the excess. Let them sit at room temperature for 20 minutes while you heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the ribs in two or three batches, about 3 minutes a side. Do not crowd the pot — you want a deep mahogany crust, not grey steamed meat. Set the ribs aside.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat and add the onions, carrots, celery, and garlic. Cook 8 to 10 minutes until the onions are soft and beginning to colour at the edges, then stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes more until it darkens to brick red.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.text: Pour in the wine, scraping every brown bit off the bottom of the pot, and simmer briskly for about 8 minutes until it has reduced by roughly a third and no longer smells sharp.

steps.title: Braise low and slow
steps.text: Return the ribs and any juices to the pot, add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves, and bring to a bare simmer. Cover and slide into the oven for 2 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours, until a fork slides into the meat with no resistance and the bones pull clean.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Lift out the ribs, strain the liquid, and skim off the fat. Simmer the sauce on the stovetop for 10 to 15 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon and leaves a clear line when you drag a finger through it. Spoon over the ribs.

tips: Chill the finished braise overnight and the fat lifts off in one solid sheet — much easier than skimming.
Serve over mashed potatoes or soft polenta. You need something to catch the sauce.
If your ribs are more bone than meat, buy an extra pound. Yield varies wildly by butcher.
recipes.cooksNote: Do not skip reducing the wine before the braise goes into the oven. Raw wine simmered under a lid for three hours stays thin and acidic in a way that no amount of finishing salt fixes, whereas eight minutes of hard reduction first cooks off the harsh edge and concentrates everything good. This is the single step that separates a decent braise from a great one.

recipes.title: Herb Butter Roast Chicken
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: A whole chicken roasted over potatoes with herb butter pushed under the skin. Shatteringly crisp.
recipes.lede: Roast chicken is the recipe I judge a cook by, and the trick is not the oven — it is the butter you work under the skin before it ever goes in. That layer bastes the breast from the inside while the potatoes underneath soak up everything that drips down. One pan, one hour and a half, and dinner looks like you tried much harder than you did.

items.name: whole chicken
items.note: about 4 lb / 1.8 kg, patted very dry

steps.title: Make the herb butter
steps.text: Mash the softened butter with the garlic, thyme, rosemary, lemon zest, and a big pinch each of salt and pepper until it is completely uniform and smells like the inside of a good restaurant.

steps.title: Get it under the skin
steps.text: Slide your fingers between the breast skin and the meat to loosen a pocket on each side, working carefully so you do not tear it. Push two-thirds of the butter in there and spread it flat from the outside; rub the rest over the whole bird.

steps.title: Season and stuff
steps.text: Salt the chicken inside and out, tuck the spent lemon halves into the cavity, and tie the legs together with kitchen twine. Let it sit while the oven heats to 425°F (220°C).

steps.title: Build the bed
steps.text: Toss the potatoes and onion with the olive oil and salt, spread them in a roasting pan or oven-safe skillet, pour in the stock, and set the chicken breast-up on top so the drippings land on the vegetables.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast for 45 minutes, then lower to 375°F (190°C) and continue 35 to 40 minutes more. It is done when the skin is deep gold and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F (74°C) without touching bone.

steps.title: Rest before carving
steps.text: Move the chicken to a board and let it rest at least 15 minutes — cutting early dumps all the juice onto the board. Toss the potatoes in the pan juices while you wait, then carve and serve everything together.

tips: Dry skin is crisp skin. If you have time, salt the bird and leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight.
No twine? Cross the ankles and tuck them under the skin flap. Close enough.
Save the carcass. It makes better stock than anything you can buy.
recipes.cooksNote: Trust the thermometer and not the clock, because a 4-pound bird and a 5-pound bird are twenty minutes apart and ovens lie by as much as 25 degrees. Check the thigh at the 70-minute mark and then every 10 minutes after. If the breast is browning faster than the legs are cooking, tent a piece of foil loosely over it and carry on.

recipes.title: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Yogurt-marinated chicken layered under saffron basmati and steamed sealed until every grain is separate.
recipes.lede: Biryani is a project and I will not pretend otherwise, but it is the kind of project that makes a table go quiet. The chicken marinates in spiced yogurt, the rice is parboiled to exactly seventy percent, and then the two steam together under a sealed lid so the meat perfumes the grain. Get the rice timing right and everything else follows.

items.name: bone-in chicken thighs
items.note: skin removed, slashed to the bone

items.name: saffron threads
items.note: a generous pinch, steeped in the warm milk

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Whisk the yogurt with the ginger-garlic paste, chile powder, turmeric, garam masala, and a heavy pinch of salt, then turn the chicken through it until every slash is coated. Leave at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions over medium heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring often, until they are a deep even brown and crisp at the edges. Lift half out onto paper towel — those are your garnish.

steps.title: Parboil the rice
steps.text: Boil a large pot of well-salted water and cook the drained rice for 5 to 6 minutes only. It is ready when a grain snaps cleanly between your fingers but still has a hard white core — about seventy percent done. Drain immediately.

steps.title: Cook the chicken down
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and all its yogurt to the pot with the remaining onions and cook uncovered over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens and pools of ghee separate at the edges.

steps.title: Layer it up
steps.text: Spread the rice evenly over the chicken without stirring. Scatter the mint, cilantro, and reserved fried onions on top, then drizzle the saffron milk across the surface in stripes so the finished rice is mottled orange and white.

steps.title: Seal and steam
steps.text: Cover with a tight lid, wrapping the rim in foil or a damp towel if it does not seal well. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, then rest off the heat 10 minutes more. The rice is done when the top grains are fully tender and steam rushes out as you lift the lid.

steps.title: Serve from the bottom up
steps.text: Dig straight down to the base with a wide spoon and lift, bringing chicken and sauce up through the rice rather than stirring it in. Serve with cool yogurt raita.

tips: Aged basmati is worth hunting down — it absorbs less water and stays separate under the steam.
Fry the onions further than feels comfortable. Pale onions taste of nothing here.
A heat diffuser or an empty skillet under the pot stops the bottom layer scorching.
Leftovers reheat beautifully with a splash of water and a covered pan.
recipes.cooksNote: The parboil is the whole recipe in one step. Rice that goes into the pot fully cooked turns to paste under twenty-five minutes of steam, and rice pulled too early stays chalky at the core because there is not enough liquid left in the pot to save it. Start testing grains at four minutes and pull the pot the moment the snap goes from brittle to just-yielding.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Lemon Herb Salmon
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: A whole side of salmon roasted low and slow under lemon, dill, and olive oil until it flakes in silky sheets.
recipes.lede: High heat is how most people ruin salmon — it seizes, weeps that white albumin, and goes dry in the thin end before the thick end is done. Cook it at 275°F instead and it stays translucent and buttery the whole way across. It is the most forgiving fish recipe I know and it takes fifteen minutes of actual work.

items.name: skin-on salmon fillet
items.note: one whole side, pin bones removed

items.name: lemons
items.note: one sliced thin, one for juice

steps.title: Heat the oven low
steps.text: Set the oven to 275°F (135°C) and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment. Take the salmon out of the fridge now so it loses its chill while the oven comes up.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Combine the olive oil, the juice of one lemon, the Dijon, honey, sliced garlic, dill, and parsley in a bowl and whisk until it emulsifies into a loose, cloudy dressing. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Dress the fish
steps.text: Lay the salmon skin-side down on the pan, pat the surface dry, and salt it well. Spoon two-thirds of the dressing over the top and spread it right to the edges, then shingle the lemon slices along the length.

steps.title: Roast gently
steps.text: Roast for 25 to 30 minutes. It is done when the thickest part flakes into wide sheets under gentle pressure from a fork and an instant-read thermometer reads 125°F (52°C) — the center should still look slightly translucent.

steps.title: Finish and rest
steps.text: Scatter the capers and remaining dressing over the hot fish and let it sit 5 minutes. Carryover heat finishes the center without pushing it past that silky stage.

steps.title: Serve in slabs
steps.text: Cut down through the flesh to the skin in wide portions and lift them off with a fish spatula, leaving the skin behind on the pan. Finish with dill sprigs and a squeeze of the second lemon.

tips: Buy centre-cut if you can. An even thickness means an evenly cooked side.
If the fillet tapers badly, tuck the thin tail end under itself so it does not overcook.
Leftovers are better cold than reheated — flake them into a salad the next day.
recipes.cooksNote: White albumin curds on the surface are the fish telling you the heat is too high, and at 275°F you will barely see any. If yours still weeps a little, the fillet was probably cold to the core going in; twenty minutes on the counter first fixes it. And pull the pan at 125°F even if it looks underdone — five minutes of resting carries it exactly where you want it.

recipes.title: Sunday Braised Beef Stew
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Chuck, carrots, and potatoes stewed three hours in red wine until a spoon is the only utensil you need.
recipes.lede: The whole argument for this stew is chuck. Not stew meat from a tray, not sirloin, not anything lean — chuck, cut into big two-inch chunks that can take three hours without falling apart into threads. Brown it properly, add the vegetables late so they do not dissolve, and you get a pot that feeds eight people and tastes better the next day.

steps.title: Dry and dredge
steps.text: Pat the beef completely dry, season hard with salt and pepper, and toss with the flour until each chunk wears a thin dusty coat. Wet meat will not brown, so this step is not optional.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot until it shimmers and brown the beef in three batches, about 6 to 8 minutes per batch, turning only once a side has released and formed a hard dark crust. Set aside.

steps.title: Sweat the aromatics
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the onions and cook 6 to 8 minutes until soft and translucent, then the garlic for 1 minute and the tomato paste for 2 minutes more, until it darkens and smells sweet rather than tinny.

steps.title: Deglaze and simmer
steps.text: Pour in the wine and scrape the pot clean, letting it bubble down by half, about 5 minutes. Return the beef with the stock and bay leaves, bring to a bare simmer, and cover. Cook 1 hour 45 minutes at the barest bubble.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the carrots and potatoes and continue, covered, for 40 to 45 minutes. Everything is ready when a knife slides into a potato with no resistance and the beef shreds under the side of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish and season
steps.text: Fish out the bay leaves, stir in the frozen peas, and let them warm through off the heat for 3 minutes. Taste and correct the salt — a long braise almost always needs more than you expect.

tips: Two-inch chunks, not one. Small pieces turn to string over three hours.
If the sauce is thin at the end, ladle a cup into a pan and reduce it hard, then stir it back.
A splash of red wine vinegar right before serving wakes the whole pot up.
recipes.cooksNote: Keep it at a lazy bubble, never a rolling boil. Boiling squeezes the collagen out of the chuck faster than it can turn to gelatin, and you end up with dry, stringy meat swimming in thin liquid — the exact failure most people blame on the cut. If the surface is doing more than blipping every couple of seconds, drop the heat or move the covered pot to a 325°F oven, where the temperature holds itself.

recipes.title: Chicken and Chorizo Seafood Paella
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Saffron rice cooked flat in one wide pan with chicken, chorizo, shrimp, and mussels — crust and all.
recipes.lede: Paella is a rice dish, not a seafood dish, and once you accept that everything gets easier. The goal is a thin flat layer of grain that absorbs the stock without ever being stirred, so the bottom catches into the crisp caramelised socarrat that people fight over. Wide pan, medium heat, hands off.

items.name: chicken stock
items.note: kept hot on a back burner

items.name: saffron threads
items.note: a generous pinch, crumbled into the stock

steps.title: Warm the stock
steps.text: Bring the stock to a simmer with the crumbled saffron and hold it there. Cold stock hitting hot rice stalls the cook and gives you unevenly done grains.

steps.title: Brown the meats
steps.text: Heat the oil in a 15-inch paella pan or wide skillet over medium-high and brown the chicken 6 to 8 minutes until golden on all sides. Add the chorizo for 2 minutes more, until its orange fat runs out into the pan, then push everything to the rim.

steps.title: Build the sofrito
steps.text: Add the onion, pepper, and garlic and cook 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Stir in the smoked paprika and the grated tomato and cook another 6 to 8 minutes, until the mixture darkens to a jammy paste and the oil separates around the edges.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Scatter the rice evenly across the pan and stir it through the sofrito for about 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and slightly translucent at the edges. Level it flat — this is the last time you stir.

steps.title: Add stock and leave it alone
steps.text: Pour in the hot stock, season, and shake the pan to settle everything. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 18 minutes without stirring, rotating the pan occasionally so it cooks evenly across the burner.

steps.title: Nestle in the seafood
steps.text: Press the shrimp and mussels into the rice and scatter over the peas. Cook 6 to 8 minutes more, until the mussels have opened, the shrimp are pink and opaque, and the surface liquid is gone. Discard any mussel that stayed shut.

steps.title: Chase the socarrat
steps.text: Turn the heat to high for 60 to 90 seconds and listen — you want a sharp crackle and a toasted smell, not a burnt one. Pull it off the heat, cover with a towel, and rest 5 minutes before serving from the pan.

tips: Widest pan you own. Rice deeper than about half an inch steams instead of roasting.
If your burner is smaller than the pan, rotate it a quarter turn every few minutes.
Bomba rice absorbs about three times its volume — that ratio is why the recipe works.
recipes.cooksNote: Not stirring is the hardest part for anyone who learned to cook risotto, but stirring is exactly what stops paella from working: it releases starch, turns the rice creamy, and guarantees you never get a socarrat. Set the spoon down after you level the rice. The only movements allowed from that point are shaking and rotating the pan.

recipes.title: Ginger Scallion Shrimp Fried Rice
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Cold leftover rice fried hard with shrimp, egg, and a heavy hand of ginger. Twenty minutes, one pan.
recipes.lede: Fried rice is the recipe that punishes you for being organised — it needs day-old rice, dried out and cold from the fridge, so the grains stay separate instead of steaming into mush. Everything else is speed. Have every ingredient chopped and sitting by the stove before the pan gets hot, because once it starts there is no time to go looking for the soy sauce.

steps.title: Set up first
steps.text: Break the cold rice apart with wet hands until there are no clumps, and line up every other ingredient in bowls next to the stove. The cooking takes eight minutes and there is no pausing once you start.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high until it just smokes, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble for about 45 seconds until barely set and still glossy. Tip them out onto a plate.

steps.title: Sear the shrimp
steps.text: Add another tablespoon of oil and spread the shrimp in a single layer. Cook 1 to 2 minutes per side, until they curl loosely into a C shape and turn opaque with pink edges, then move them out with the eggs. A tight O means overcooked.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
steps.text: Add the last of the oil with the ginger, garlic, and scallion whites and stir constantly for 30 seconds — just until fragrant and sizzling, before the garlic takes any colour. Toss in the frozen peas and carrots for a minute.

steps.title: Fry the rice hard
steps.text: Add the rice and press it against the pan, letting it sit 30 seconds between tosses. Keep going for 4 to 5 minutes until the grains are separate, hot through, and you hear them popping against the metal.

steps.title: Bring it back together
steps.text: Drizzle the soy and oyster sauce down the side of the pan so they hit hot metal and caramelise, then fold in the eggs, shrimp, and scallion greens. Off the heat, add the sesame oil and white pepper, taste, and serve immediately.

tips: No day-old rice? Spread fresh rice on a sheet pan and freeze it uncovered for 30 minutes.
Cook in two batches if your pan is small. Crowded rice steams and never crisps.
Sauce down the hot side of the pan, never straight onto the rice — that is where the smoky flavour comes from.
recipes.cooksNote: Your burner is almost certainly weaker than a restaurant wok range, so the fix is to stop treating it like a stir-fry and let the rice sit still. Pressing a layer flat and leaving it undisturbed for thirty seconds at a time builds far more browning than constant tossing does on a home stove. Loud and a little scary is the correct sound.

recipes.title: Blistered Basil Drunken Noodles
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Wide rice noodles charred in a hot wok with pork, chilies and a fistful of holy basil.
recipes.lede: This is the noodle dish I make when the day has been long and I want dinner to taste like it came from a street cart. The whole thing lives or dies on heat, so get the pan hotter than feels reasonable and don't crowd it. Everything else is stirring, and it's over in twelve minutes.

items.name: palm sugar or light brown sugar
Thai holy basil leaves, loosely packed
items.note: Italian basil works in a pinch

steps.title: Loosen the noodles
steps.text: If the fresh noodles came refrigerated and welded into a block, microwave them in 30-second bursts until they are warm and slack, then peel the ribbons apart with your fingers. They should bend without cracking; a noodle that snaps will shatter in the wok.

steps.title: Stir the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, dark soy and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar has dissolved completely and no grit is left at the bottom. Set it right next to the stove, because once you start cooking there is no time to go looking for it.

steps.title: Prep everything within arm's reach
steps.text: Line up the garlic, chilies, pork, Chinese broccoli stems, leaves and basil in the order you will add them. This dish moves faster than you can chop, so mise en place is not optional here.

steps.title: Get the wok smoking
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or the widest skillet you own over the highest heat until it shimmers and a drop of water flicked in vanishes instantly. Add the garlic and chilies and stir for about 15 seconds, just until the garlic turns pale gold and smells sharp.

steps.title: Brown the pork
steps.text: Add the pork and press it flat against the pan, letting it sit undisturbed for a full minute before breaking it up. Cook until the pork is browned in spots and no longer pink, about 2 minutes total, then add the Chinese broccoli stems and toss for another minute until they turn bright green.

steps.title: Char the noodles
steps.text: Add the noodles and the sauce and toss with a spatula, scraping from the bottom, for 2 to 3 minutes. You want some ribbons to blister and darken where they touch the metal, which is the whole point of the dish, so resist the urge to stir constantly.

steps.title: Finish with basil
steps.text: Kill the heat, throw in the Chinese broccoli leaves and all the basil, and fold twice. The basil should wilt from residual heat alone and still look green. Serve immediately with lime wedges, straight from the pan.

tips: Fresh noodles are worth hunting down, but dried wide rice noodles work: soak them in hot tap water for 30 minutes until pliable, never boil them.
If your stove is weak, cook this in two batches. A crowded wok steams the noodles and you lose the char entirely.
Holy basil has a peppery, almost clove-like edge. Thai sweet basil is the next best thing; Italian basil is a distant but acceptable third.
recipes.cooksNote: The name comes from the idea that this is what you want at the end of a long night, and honestly, that tracks. Four chilies makes it genuinely hot. Two makes it a dish everyone at the table will eat, and there is no shame in that; I usually cook it mild and put a dish of sliced chilies in fish sauce on the table so people can escalate on their own terms.

recipes.title: Weeknight Tamarind Pad Thai
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Properly sour, properly sweet, and nothing like the ketchup-red version you get at the mall.
recipes.lede: Real pad thai is sour first, sweet second, and salty underneath, and once you taste that balance you cannot go back to the orange stuff. The only ingredient you may have to order is tamarind concentrate, and one jar will last you a year of these. Soak the noodles while you chop and the cooking is over in fifteen minutes.

items.name: tamarind concentrate
items.note: the dark, sour paste, not sweetened syrup

items.name: palm sugar, chopped, or light brown sugar
bean sprouts
items.note: half for the pan, half raw on top

steps.title: Soak the noodles
steps.text: Cover the dried noodles with warm tap water and leave them for 25 to 30 minutes while you prep everything else. They are ready when a strand bends into a full circle without breaking but still feels chalky and firm in the middle; they finish cooking in the pan.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Warm the tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until the sugar melts and the mixture is smooth and glossy, about 2 minutes. Taste it: it should be aggressively sour and salty, because it will be spread across a pound of noodles.

steps.title: Crisp the tofu
steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and fry the tofu, undisturbed, until the undersides are deep gold, about 3 minutes, then turn and repeat. Scoop it onto a plate and leave the oil behind.

steps.title: Cook the shrimp and aromatics
steps.text: Add the last tablespoon of oil, then the garlic and shallot, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook until they curl into loose C-shapes and turn opaque, about 2 minutes, then push everything to one side of the pan.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Crack the eggs into the empty side of the pan, break the yolks, and let them set for about 30 seconds before scrambling them into soft curds. Do not fully cook them; they should still look slightly wet when you move on.

steps.title: Toss in the noodles
steps.text: Drain the noodles well and add them with all of the sauce. Toss constantly for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles have drunk up the sauce, turned an even mahogany brown, and gone completely tender with no chalky centre.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fold in the tofu, the garlic chives and half the bean sprouts and toss for 30 seconds, just until the sprouts lose their raw edge but still snap. Pile onto plates and top with the remaining raw sprouts, the peanuts and a lime wedge each.

tips: Taste the sauce before it hits the noodles. Tamarind brands vary wildly in sourness, so adjust with a little more sugar or a squeeze of lime until it makes you squint slightly.
Soak, never boil, the noodles. Boiled rice noodles turn to paste the moment they meet a hot pan.
No shrimp? Sliced chicken thigh works beautifully; give it 4 minutes instead of 2 and cook it through before the eggs go in.
recipes.cooksNote: I make this in two batches when I am cooking for more than four, because a pan packed with noodles steams instead of frying and you end up with something soft and sad. Keep the first batch warm in a low oven, wipe the pan, and go again. It takes an extra six minutes and it is the difference between a good pad thai and a great one.

recipes.title: Miso Butter Chicken Ramen
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: A rich, savoury broth built in an hour, with butter melted in at the end for body.
recipes.lede: Proper ramen shops simmer bones for two days, and I respect that, but I am not doing it on a Tuesday. This version leans on chicken thighs, dried shiitake and white miso to get somewhere genuinely deep in about an hour, and a knob of butter whisked in at the end gives it the mouthfeel that usually takes all that time.

steps.title: Start the broth
steps.text: Put the stock, chicken thighs and dried shiitake in a large pot, bring it to a bare simmer, and skim off the grey foam that rises in the first five minutes. Keep it at the barest bubble for 35 minutes, until the chicken pulls away from the bone with almost no resistance.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: While the broth simmers, lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water and cook for exactly 7 minutes, then plunge them into ice water. Peel them once they are cold to the touch; the yolks should be set at the edge and jammy in the centre.

steps.title: Shred the chicken
steps.text: Lift the thighs and mushrooms out of the broth. When the chicken is cool enough to handle, pull the meat off in big shreds and discard the skin and bones. Slice the softened shiitake caps thinly and put both aside.

steps.title: Season the broth
steps.text: Whisk the garlic, ginger, miso, soy sauce and sesame oil into a ladleful of hot broth in a bowl until completely smooth, then stir that slurry back into the pot. Never dump miso straight into the pot or you will chase lumps around for ten minutes.

steps.title: Mount the butter
steps.text: Take the pot off direct heat and whisk in the cold butter a cube at a time until the broth turns slightly opaque and glossy and no fat is pooling on the surface. Taste and add soy sauce if it needs more salt; it should taste a shade too strong on its own.

steps.title: Cook the noodles separately
steps.text: Boil the ramen noodles in a separate pot of unsalted water according to the package, usually 90 seconds to 2 minutes, until they are springy with no raw core. Drain them well so you are not watering down the broth you just built.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Divide the noodles among four deep bowls and ladle the hot broth over. Top each with shredded chicken, sliced shiitake, a halved egg, scallions, a piece of nori tucked against the rim, and as much chili crisp as you want. Eat immediately.

tips: Never boil the broth after the miso goes in. High heat makes miso grainy and dulls its flavour; keep it just below a simmer.
Cook the noodles in their own pot every single time. Starch from the noodles will turn your broth cloudy and gluey.
The broth keeps for four days in the fridge and freezes for three months. Freeze it before the butter goes in and mount it fresh when you reheat.
recipes.cooksNote: The butter is not a gimmick. Miso and butter share a savoury, slightly funky wavelength, and the fat emulsified into the broth gives you that clinging, lip-coating quality that a quick stock normally lacks. If you are dairy-free, a tablespoon of tahini whisked in does a surprisingly similar job.

recipes.title: Deep Winter Minestrone
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Pancetta, beans, kale and a Parmesan rind simmered until the whole pot tastes like one thing.
recipes.lede: Minestrone has a reputation as the soup you make from whatever is dying in the crisper, and it can be, but the version worth eating has a spine: pancetta, tomato paste cooked until it darkens, and a Parmesan rind sitting in the pot the whole time. It is better on the second day and it freezes like a dream.

items.name: lacinato kale, stemmed and roughly chopped

steps.title: Render the pancetta
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the pancetta. Cook, stirring now and then, for 6 to 8 minutes until the fat has rendered out and the pieces are crisp at the edges and golden but not hard.

steps.title: Sweat the soffritto
steps.text: Add the onion, carrot and celery with a good pinch of salt and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is fully translucent and the carrots have lost their raw crunch. Rushing this step is the single most common way minestrone ends up tasting thin.

steps.title: Darken the tomato paste
steps.text: Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomato paste and keep stirring for 2 to 3 minutes until it turns from bright red to a deep brick colour and starts sticking to the bottom of the pot. That fond is flavour; it will lift when the liquid goes in.

steps.title: Simmer with the rind
steps.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stock, scraping the bottom clean, and drop in the Parmesan rind. Bring it to a simmer and cook, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the broth has darkened and tastes savoury rather than sharply tomatoey.

steps.title: Add beans and greens
steps.text: Stir in the beans and the kale and simmer for another 10 minutes, until the kale is completely tender and has gone a deep, dark green with no squeak left in it.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Add the pasta and simmer for the time on the package, usually 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick to the bottom. Fish out the Parmesan rind, taste hard for salt, and adjust. The soup should be thick enough that a spoon leaves a brief trail.

tips: Save every Parmesan rind you ever finish in a bag in the freezer. They cost nothing and they do more for a pot of soup than an extra hour of simmering.
If you are making this to eat over several days, cook the pasta separately and add it to each bowl. Pasta left in the pot overnight swells up and drinks the broth.
Skip the pancetta and use an extra glug of olive oil plus a teaspoon of smoked paprika for a vegetarian version with the same backbone.
recipes.cooksNote: There is a moment near the end where the soup stops tasting like a list of vegetables and starts tasting like minestrone, and it usually arrives about ten minutes after you think it is done. If it still tastes like separate ingredients, give it another quarter hour on low. Finish every bowl with olive oil and grated Parmesan.

recipes.title: Charred Tomato and Fennel Soup
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Tomatoes roasted hard until they blacken, blended smooth with fennel and a little cream.
recipes.lede: Tomato soup made from raw tomatoes tastes like watery ketchup, so I roast them at high heat until the edges actually blacken and the sugars concentrate. Fennel is the ingredient nobody expects, and it turns the whole thing rounder and slightly sweet. This is the one I serve with a grilled cheese and no apology.

items.name: fennel bulb, cored and thickly sliced

steps.title: Heat the oven hard
steps.text: Set the oven to 425F (220C) and put a rack in the upper third. A hot oven and a high rack are what give you char instead of stewed vegetables, so do not compromise on either.

steps.title: Toss and roast
steps.text: Spread the tomatoes cut side up on a large sheet pan with the fennel, onion and unpeeled garlic, drizzle with the olive oil, and season generously with salt and pepper. Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, until the tomato skins are wrinkled and blistered black in patches and the fennel edges are deep brown.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: While the vegetables roast, warm a tablespoon of oil in a soup pot over medium heat and add the tomato paste, crushed fennel seeds and pepper flakes. Stir for 2 minutes until the paste darkens to brick red and the kitchen smells like anise.

steps.title: Combine and simmer
steps.text: Squeeze the garlic out of its skins into the pot and scrape in everything from the sheet pan, including any dark syrupy juices, which hold most of the flavour. Add the stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes so the roasted flavours settle into the liquid.

steps.title: Blend until velvety
steps.text: Add the basil and blend, in batches in a standing blender or with an immersion blender, until the soup is completely smooth with no flecks of skin left, about 60 seconds of hard blending. Loosen with a splash more stock if it is thicker than you like.

steps.title: Finish with cream and acid
steps.text: Return the soup to low heat, stir in the cream and the sherry vinegar, and warm through without boiling. Taste and keep adding salt in small pinches until the tomato flavour suddenly jumps forward; that is the point where it is seasoned. Serve topped with the reserved fennel fronds.

tips: Out of season, canned whole tomatoes actually beat sad fresh ones. Drain two 28-ounce cans and roast them exactly the same way.
Blend hot soup in batches no more than half full, with the blender lid cracked and a towel over the top. A sealed blender of hot liquid will erupt.
For a dairy-free version, swap the cream for full-fat coconut milk. It reads as richness, not coconut, once the tomato and fennel are in play.
recipes.cooksNote: The vinegar at the end is doing more work than the cream. Roasted tomatoes turn deeply sweet, and without something sharp to cut against, the soup tastes flat in a way that more salt will not fix. If you only have lemon, use that, but add it off the heat so it stays bright.

recipes.title: Sunday Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: A whole chicken poached into its own broth, with egg noodles and a lot of dill.
recipes.lede: Every shortcut version of this soup tastes like salty water with chicken in it, and the reason is that the broth was never made from the bird. Poach a whole chicken gently for an hour and you get stock and meat in one pot, which is the entire trick. The dill at the end is not optional in my kitchen.

items.name: yellow onion, halved through the root
carrots
items.note: 2 halved for the broth, 2 sliced for the soup

items.name: celery stalks
items.note: 2 halved for the broth, 2 sliced for the soup

steps.title: Start the chicken cold
steps.text: Put the whole chicken in a large stockpot and cover with the cold water. Starting cold draws more flavour out of the bird; dropping it into boiling water seizes the proteins and gives you a cloudy, weaker broth.

steps.title: Skim and simmer
steps.text: Bring it slowly up to heat and, as the surface foams, skim off the grey scum with a spoon until it stops appearing, about 8 minutes. Add the onion, the halved carrots and celery, bay leaves, peppercorns and thyme, and keep it at a lazy simmer with barely a bubble breaking the surface.

steps.title: Poach until tender
steps.text: Cook uncovered for 60 to 70 minutes, never letting it boil, until a leg twists away from the body with almost no effort and the thigh meat reads 175F (80C). Lift the chicken out onto a tray and let it cool enough to handle.

steps.title: Strain and clean the broth
steps.text: Pour the broth through a fine sieve into a clean pot and discard the spent vegetables and herbs, which have given up everything they have. Let it settle for a few minutes, then skim the fat from the surface, leaving a thin golden slick behind for richness.

steps.title: Pull the meat
steps.text: Pull the skin off the chicken and shred the meat into generous bite-sized pieces, discarding bones and cartilage. You should end up with roughly four cups; save any you do not use for sandwiches.

steps.title: Cook the fresh vegetables
steps.text: Bring the strained broth back to a simmer, add the butter and the sliced carrots and celery, and cook for 8 minutes until the carrots are tender at the edge but still hold their shape when you bite one.

steps.title: Noodles last
steps.text: Add the egg noodles and cook until just tender, 6 to 8 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken, the dill, parsley and lemon juice. Salt it far more assertively than you think you need to, tasting after each addition until the broth tastes like chicken rather than like hot water.

tips: The broth will taste like nothing until you salt it properly. Unsalted homemade stock always does, so keep going in half-teaspoon increments until it clicks.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot if you plan on leftovers. Overnight in the fridge they will drink the broth and turn the soup into a casserole.
Roast the chicken bones for 20 minutes before adding the water if you want a darker, richer broth. It adds half an hour and a lot of depth.
recipes.cooksNote: If someone in the house is actually sick, add a thumb of smashed ginger and two extra garlic cloves to the broth while it simmers, and finish with more lemon. It does not cure anything, but it is warm and sharp and it makes people feel looked after, which is most of what this soup is for anyway.

recipes.title: Charred Romaine Caesar with Rye Crumbs
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Romaine hearts seared until smoky, with a real anchovy dressing and torn rye croutons.
recipes.lede: A Caesar is only as good as its anchovies, and if you tell me you do not like anchovies I will tell you that you have been eating Caesars without them. Charring the romaine over high heat gives the leaves a smoky edge that stands up to the dressing instead of collapsing under it. Rye croutons instead of white bread, because they taste like something.

items.name: day-old rye bread, torn into rough pieces

steps.title: Toast the rye crumbs
steps.text: Toss the torn rye with the olive oil and a pinch of salt and spread it on a sheet pan. Bake at 375F (190C) for 12 to 15 minutes, tossing once, until the pieces are dry all the way through and crack rather than bend when you squeeze one.

steps.title: Make an anchovy paste
steps.text: Chop the anchovies and garlic together on a board, then drag the flat of the knife across the pile repeatedly until it becomes a smooth grey-brown paste with no visible fibres. This is the step that stops anyone finding a whole anchovy in their mouth.

steps.title: Start the emulsion
steps.text: Whisk the paste with the egg yolk, Dijon, lemon juice and Worcestershire in a bowl until the mixture is uniform and slightly frothy. Set the bowl on a damp towel so it stays put while you pour.

steps.title: Stream in the oil
steps.text: Add the oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly, then in a thin steady stream once it starts to thicken. Stop when the dressing is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon and holds a faint ribbon on the surface, then whisk in the grated Parmesan.

steps.title: Char the romaine
steps.text: Get a grill pan or heavy skillet very hot, brush the cut faces of the romaine with a little oil, and lay them down cut side first. Leave them completely alone for 90 seconds to 2 minutes, until the cut face is streaked black and the outer leaves have just started to wilt.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Lay the charred halves cut side up on a platter, spoon the dressing along the length of each so it runs down between the leaves, and scatter the rye crumbs and shaved Parmesan over the top. Finish with a lot of black pepper and serve while the lettuce is still warm at the base.

tips: If a raw yolk worries you, use a pasteurized egg or start from 3 tablespoons of good mayonnaise and whisk the flavourings into that instead.
The dressing keeps for three days in the fridge. It will thicken up, so loosen it with a teaspoon of water before using.
Do not walk away from the romaine on the pan. There is about thirty seconds between beautifully charred and collapsed and bitter.
recipes.cooksNote: Six anchovies sounds like a lot and it is exactly right. They dissolve completely into the dressing and what you taste is not fish, it is savoury depth, the same thing Worcestershire and Parmesan are doing from the other direction. Buy the ones packed in oil in glass jars if you can; the flat tins are usually saltier and coarser.

recipes.title: Lemon Farro Salad with Feta and Herbs
recipes.author: Mom
recipes.desc: Chewy farro tossed warm with lemon, half a garden of herbs, feta and toasted pistachios.
recipes.lede: This is the salad I bring to other people's houses, because it travels well, it does not wilt, and it somehow gets better sitting on a table for an hour. The important move is dressing the farro while it is still hot so the grains actually absorb the lemon instead of just wearing it. Do not be shy with the herbs; they are a vegetable here, not a garnish.

items.name: kosher salt
items.note: for the cooking water and to taste

items.name: feta, crumbled
items.note: block feta in brine, not pre-crumbled

steps.title: Cook the farro like pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and add the farro. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the grains are tender but still push back with a distinct chew; they should never go soft and split. Drain but do not rinse.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: While the farro cooks, whisk the lemon zest and juice, olive oil, honey and grated garlic in a large serving bowl with a good pinch of salt until it thickens slightly and stops separating on the whisk.

steps.title: Dress it hot
steps.text: Tip the hot drained farro straight into the bowl with the dressing and toss well. Let it sit for 10 minutes, stirring once, until the grains have drunk up most of the liquid and look glossy rather than wet at the bottom of the bowl.

steps.title: Toast the pistachios
steps.text: Toast the pistachios in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking often, for 3 to 4 minutes until they smell nutty and have taken on a shade of colour. Tip them onto a plate immediately, because they will keep browning in a hot pan.

steps.title: Fold in the fresh things
steps.text: Once the farro is only just warm, add the cucumber, tomatoes and scallions and fold gently. Adding these to hot grains will cook the cucumber and turn it limp, so give it the extra few minutes.

steps.title: Finish with herbs and feta
steps.text: Add the dill, mint, most of the feta and most of the pistachios and toss lightly, keeping some texture rather than mashing everything together. Taste for salt and lemon, scatter the reserved feta and nuts over the top, and grind over plenty of black pepper.

tips: Pearled farro cooks in about 25 minutes. Whole or semi-pearled needs 40 minutes and an overnight soak, so check the bag before you plan around it.
Make the farro base up to two days ahead and keep it in the fridge, but hold the herbs, feta and nuts until an hour before serving.
Salt the cooking water like pasta water. Grains seasoned only at the end always taste faintly bland in the middle.
recipes.cooksNote: Grain salads go wrong when the grain is treated as filler. Farro has real nuttiness and a chew that stands up to a sharp dressing, which is why it works here and why quinoa, for all its virtues, does not do the same job. If you cannot find farro, use barley or freekeh before you reach for anything smaller.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Olive Oil Cake
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: A deep, damp chocolate cake made with olive oil instead of butter — no mixer, one bowl, better on day two.
recipes.lede: I stopped making butter chocolate cake the year I started making this one. Olive oil keeps the crumb damp for three full days where butter goes stiff overnight, and a good grassy oil pushes the cocoa somewhere darker and more grown-up. It comes together in one bowl with a whisk, which is the real reason I make it on weeknights.

items.name: extra-virgin olive oil
items.note: a fruity one, not a bitter one

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Set a rack in the center of the oven and heat it to 350F (175C). Oil a 9-inch round cake pan, line the bottom with a parchment circle, and oil the parchment too — this cake is wet enough that it will grip a bare pan.

steps.title: Whisk the dry ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk the flour, cocoa, sugar, baking soda and fine salt for a full 30 seconds. Cocoa clumps hide well, so keep going until the mixture is one even shade of brown with no dark specks.

steps.title: Add the wet ingredients
steps.text: Pour in the olive oil, hot coffee, milk, eggs, vanilla and vinegar. Whisk from the center outward until the batter is glossy and completely smooth — it will be much looser than a butter cake batter, closer to heavy cream, and that is exactly right.

steps.title: Fold in the chocolate
steps.text: Stir in the chopped chocolate with a spatula, using no more than ten strokes. Stop the moment the pieces are distributed; overworking now is what gives you a tight, rubbery crumb later.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour into the pan and bake 38 to 42 minutes, until the top has domed and lost its shine and a skewer in the very center comes out with a few moist crumbs clinging to it. A clean skewer means you have gone too far by about four minutes.

steps.title: Cool and finish
steps.text: Cool in the pan on a rack for 20 minutes, then turn out, peel off the parchment and cool right side up. Scatter flaky salt over the top while it is still slightly warm so it sticks instead of rolling off.

tips: Use a fruity, peppery olive oil you would happily put on bread. A flat supermarket oil makes a flat cake.
The coffee does not make it taste like coffee — it makes the cocoa taste more like chocolate. Hot water works, but you lose depth.
Wrapped at room temperature, this is genuinely better on day two. Never refrigerate it; the oil firms up and the crumb goes waxy.
recipes.cooksNote: If you want to dress it up, this takes a whipped creme fraiche beautifully — 1 cup cold cream whipped with 1/2 cup creme fraiche and a spoonful of sugar to soft peaks. Spread it on in thick swoops right before serving, never in advance, or the cream will weep into the cake.

recipes.title: Brown Butter Sea Salt Brownies
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Fudgy in the middle, chewy at the edge, with a shattery paper-thin top and browned butter doing the heavy lifting.
recipes.lede: Every brownie recipe promises a crackly top and most of them lie. The trick is not the chocolate, it is whipping the eggs and sugar long enough to dissolve the sugar completely — that is what forms the meringue-thin sheet on top. Browning the butter first is the other half, and it takes five extra minutes for a nutty, almost butterscotch depth under the cocoa.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat, swirling often. After about 6 minutes the foam will subside, the milk solids on the bottom will turn amber and it will smell like toasted hazelnuts — pull it off immediately and pour it, browned bits and all, over the chopped chocolate.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Let the hot butter sit on the chocolate for 2 minutes, then stir until completely smooth and glossy. Set it aside to cool for 10 minutes; if it is still hot when it meets the eggs you will scramble them.

steps.title: Heat the oven and pan
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350F (175C). Line a 9-inch square pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides so you can lift the whole slab out later.

steps.title: Whip the eggs and sugars
steps.text: Beat both sugars with the eggs, yolk and vanilla on high speed for a full 4 minutes, until the mixture is pale, thick, and falls off the beater in a ribbon that holds its shape for a second or two. This step is the crackly top — do not shorten it.

steps.title: Combine and fold
steps.text: Pour the cooled chocolate mixture down the side of the bowl and fold in gently. Sift the flour, cocoa, espresso powder and fine salt over the top and fold just until no dry streaks remain, then stop — the batter should still look thick and satiny.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake 26 to 30 minutes, until the edges are set and slightly puffed and the center barely wobbles when you nudge the pan; a toothpick 2 inches from the edge should come out with thick moist crumbs. Cool completely in the pan, at least 1 hour, before lifting out and cutting.

tips: Cut them cold. Chill the cooled slab 30 minutes and use a long knife wiped clean between cuts for edges you could photograph.
Brown the butter in a stainless or light pan. In a dark nonstick you cannot see the color change and you will burn it.
Underbaked beats overbaked here every single time. They firm up a lot as they cool.
recipes.cooksNote: The espresso powder is not there to taste of coffee — a teaspoon just sharpens the cocoa and makes the whole thing read as darker chocolate than it actually is. If you are baking for kids who object on principle, leave it out and add an extra ounce of chopped chocolate instead.

recipes.title: Peach and Blackberry Summer Galette
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: A free-form pie for people who do not want to crimp anything — buttery crust, jammy peaches, and no pie plate required.
recipes.lede: A galette is a pie that has forgiven itself. You roll the dough, pile fruit in the middle, flop the edges over and it is done — and because it bakes flat on a sheet pan, the crust actually crisps underneath instead of going pale and soft the way a deep-dish bottom does. I make this every August when peaches get so ripe they are a nuisance to eat over a plate.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt in a bowl, add the cold butter, and rub or cut it in until the largest pieces are the size of almonds and the rest is coarse and sandy. Those visible butter pieces are the flakes — do not blitz them into powder.

steps.title: Bring it together and chill
steps.text: Sprinkle the ice water over and toss with a fork until the dough holds together when you squeeze a handful, adding another spoonful of water only if it truly will not clump. Press into a disc, wrap, and chill 30 minutes until firm but not rock hard.

steps.title: Macerate the fruit
steps.text: Toss the peaches, blackberries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and cinnamon in a bowl and leave for 15 minutes. The fruit will release juice and the cornstarch will hydrate into a cloudy syrup that thickens properly in the oven.

steps.title: Roll the dough
steps.text: On a floured sheet of parchment, roll the disc into a rough 13-inch round about 1/8 inch thick. Do not chase a perfect circle — ragged edges are the whole charm. Slide the parchment onto a sheet pan.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Pile the fruit in the center, leaving a 2-inch border, and lift that border up over the filling, pleating every few inches. Leave the juices behind in the bowl — that puddle is what makes a soggy bottom.

steps.title: Wash and bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400F (200C), brush the pastry with the beaten egg and shower it with turbinado sugar. Bake 42 to 48 minutes, until the crust is deep golden brown all the way to the base and the fruit juices are bubbling thickly rather than running thin.

steps.title: Cool before cutting
steps.text: Let it sit on the pan for at least 20 minutes. The filling sets as it cools, and a galette cut hot will slide apart into a delicious mess on the board.

tips: If the dough cracks as you fold, it is too cold — wait five minutes and it will cooperate.
Nectarines, plums and apricots all work at the same weight. Berries alone need an extra tablespoon of cornstarch since they run wetter.
Bake on the lowest rack for the last 10 minutes if the bottom looks pale when you peek.
recipes.cooksNote: Leftovers reheat astonishingly well: 10 minutes at 350F on a sheet pan brings the crust right back. Do not cover it or microwave it — steam is the enemy of everything good about this pastry.
