recipes.title: Buttermilk Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Barely-set cream with a tang from buttermilk, poured into glasses and forgotten in the fridge until dessert.
recipes.lede: Straight cream panna cotta gets cloying by the fourth spoonful. Swapping in buttermilk for a good share of it adds an edge of sourness that keeps the whole thing tasting light, and it is the reason people finish the glass. I use just enough gelatin to hold a wobble — if it slices cleanly you have used too much.

steps.title: Bloom the gelatin
steps.text: Sprinkle the gelatin evenly over the cold water in a small bowl and leave it 5 minutes without stirring. It is ready when the surface has wrinkled and the whole thing feels spongy and solid, like a firm sponge, with no dry powder left.

steps.title: Warm the cream
steps.text: Combine the cream, milk, sugar, the scraped vanilla seeds and pod, and the salt in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Warm until steam rises and the edges shimmer, about 5 minutes — around 170F. Do not let it boil or the cream will taste cooked.

steps.title: Dissolve the gelatin
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the bloomed gelatin and whisk for 30 seconds until it has completely vanished. Rub a little between your fingers; if you feel any grain at all, whisk longer over gentle heat.

steps.title: Add the buttermilk
steps.text: Let the cream cool for 10 minutes, then fish out the vanilla pod and whisk in the cold buttermilk and vanilla extract. Adding buttermilk off the heat is essential — hot buttermilk splits into curds and whey and there is no coming back from that.

steps.title: Strain and pour
steps.text: Pour through a fine sieve into a measuring jug, which catches any stray gelatin threads and gives you a clean spout. Divide among 6 small glasses or ramekins and cover loosely.

steps.title: Chill until just set
steps.text: Refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight. It is ready when a tilted glass shows a surface that holds its shape for a beat and then slumps — a firm, sliceable set means too much gelatin. Serve cold with honey drizzled over and raspberries on top.

tips: Full-fat buttermilk only. Low-fat versions set thin and taste chalky against the cream.
To unmold rather than serve in glasses, oil the ramekins lightly first and dip them in hot water for 8 seconds before turning out.
Steep a strip of lemon peel or a few crushed cardamom pods in the warm cream for 15 minutes, then strain, if you want a version that feels less familiar.
recipes.cooksNote: This is the dessert I make when I am cooking a real dinner, because every bit of the work happens the day before and all that is left at the table is a spoon of honey. It holds beautifully for three days covered in the fridge; after that the surface starts to dry and toughen.

recipes.title: Iced Matcha Oat Latte
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Cafe-grade iced matcha at home — properly sifted, whisked smooth, and sweetened with a two-minute vanilla syrup.
recipes.lede: The gritty, bitter matcha most people make at home has two fixable problems: water that is too hot and powder that was never sifted. Fix both and you get something sweet, grassy and creamy that costs about a dollar a glass instead of seven. The vanilla syrup takes two minutes and keeps for a month, so make the whole batch.

items.name: oat milk
items.note: barista style if you have it

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Bring the sugar and water to a simmer in a small pan, stirring, and cook just until the liquid turns completely clear with no grain visible on the bottom, about 2 minutes. Take it off the heat, stir in the vanilla, and cool — it keeps a month in a jar in the fridge.

steps.title: Sift the matcha
steps.text: Push the matcha through a small fine-mesh sieve into a wide bowl or mug. Matcha clumps the moment it meets moisture, and sifting is the only reliable way to avoid the little bitter pellets that sink to the bottom of a glass.

steps.title: Whisk it smooth
steps.text: Add the hot water — 175F, which is a kettle brought to a boil and then left for 3 minutes — and whisk briskly in a W motion for about 20 seconds, until the surface carries a fine even foam and there is not a speck of powder clinging to the sides.

steps.title: Build the glasses
steps.text: Fill two tall glasses with ice, divide the oat milk between them, and stir in the vanilla syrup and a tiny pinch of salt. Salt in a sweet drink sounds odd but it takes the chalky edge off oat milk.

steps.title: Pour and layer
steps.text: Pour the whisked matcha slowly over the back of a spoon into each glass. It will sit in a bright green layer over the milk for a good minute, which is the entire point of making it at home.

steps.title: Stir and taste
steps.text: Stir just before drinking and taste — matcha varies enormously by harvest, so add another teaspoon of syrup if yours is sharp. Grate over a little orange zest if you want it to taste like something you paid for.

tips: Boiling water scorches matcha and turns it bitter and flat. If you have no thermometer, boil then wait three full minutes.
Buy ceremonial grade for drinking. Culinary grade is made to stand up to sugar and flour in baking and tastes harsh on its own.
Store the tin in the fridge, sealed and away from light. Matcha fades from bright green to dull olive within weeks on a warm shelf.
recipes.cooksNote: Doubling this to make a jug for a table does not work well — whisked matcha separates within about ten minutes and the foam collapses. Whisk each round of two glasses fresh; it takes under a minute once the syrup is made.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Almond Horchata
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Rice and almonds soaked overnight with canela, blended and strained twice into the creamiest pitcher drink there is.
recipes.lede: Horchata from a powder is a sad, sandy imitation of the real thing, and the real thing needs almost no work — it just needs time. You soak, you blend, you strain. The two details that matter are true Mexican canela, which is soft and floral rather than the hot red-hot cassia most jars hold, and straining twice so there is no grit.

steps.title: Toast the rice and cinnamon
steps.text: Toast the rinsed, drained rice, the almonds and the broken cinnamon in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until the rice smells nutty and a few grains have turned faintly golden. This is optional in most recipes and it is the step that makes mine taste deeper.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Tip everything into a bowl, pour over the hot water, and leave at room temperature at least 4 hours or overnight in the fridge. The rice is ready when a grain crushes easily between your fingernails with no hard core.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the soaking liquid with all the solids on high for a full 2 minutes, in batches if your blender is small. Stop when the mixture is thick, opaque and milk-white with no visible grains bouncing around the jug.

steps.title: Strain twice
steps.text: Pour through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a double layer of cheesecloth, gathering the corners and squeezing hard to get every drop. Rinse the cloth and repeat — the second pass is what takes it from slightly chalky to properly silky.

steps.title: Sweeten and season
steps.text: Whisk in the milk, condensed milk, sugar, vanilla and salt until fully dissolved. Taste now while you can still fix it: it should be a touch sweeter than you want, since ice will dilute it in the glass.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: Refrigerate until properly cold, at least 1 hour, then stir well — it separates as it stands, which is a sign you did it right. Pour over tall glasses of ice and dust with ground cinnamon.

tips: Squeeze the cheesecloth hard. Most of the body of the drink is in the last third of the liquid you extract.
Canela is worth seeking out at a Latin market. It shatters between your fingers where cassia sticks feel like bark.
Keeps 4 days covered in the fridge. Always shake or stir before pouring.
recipes.cooksNote: Do not throw away the strained pulp — stir it into pancake batter or oatmeal within a day and you get a faint almond-cinnamon sweetness for free. If you want a lighter version, skip the condensed milk entirely and take the sugar up to 1/3 cup; it will taste cleaner and less like dessert.

recipes.title: Blistered Garlic Green Beans
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Green beans left alone in a screaming hot pan until they char, then finished with sliced garlic, chile and lemon.
recipes.lede: Steamed green beans are a side dish nobody remembers. Blistered ones — cooked in a pan hot enough to blacken them in patches — get sweet and smoky and disappear off the platter first. The whole trick is that you must not stir for the first three minutes, which is genuinely the hardest instruction in this recipe.

steps.title: Dry the beans properly
steps.text: Wash the beans well ahead and dry them on a towel until there is not a bead of water left. Wet beans steam instead of blistering, and steaming is exactly what you are trying to avoid here.

steps.title: Get the pan hot
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in your largest skillet over medium-high until it shimmers and moves like water when you tilt the pan, about 2 minutes. Cast iron or stainless beats nonstick, which cannot safely get hot enough.

steps.title: Blister without touching
steps.text: Add the beans in as close to a single layer as you can, season with the kosher salt, and leave them completely alone for 3 to 4 minutes. They are ready to move when the undersides show dark brown and black blisters and the pan smells toasty.

steps.title: Toss and finish cooking
steps.text: Toss and continue cooking 4 to 5 minutes more, tossing only every minute or so, until the beans are blistered in patches all over and crisp-tender — bend one, and it should droop slightly but still snap if you push it.

steps.title: Add the garlic and chile
steps.text: Push the beans to one side, drop the butter into the clear space with the sliced garlic and pepper flakes, and cook 45 seconds until the garlic is fragrant and just turning pale gold. Any darker and it goes bitter, so toss everything together the second it colors.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Off the heat, add the lemon zest, lemon juice and black pepper and toss hard. Tip onto a platter and scatter over the toasted almonds and Parmesan. Serve immediately, while the beans are still squeaky.

tips: Cook in two batches if your pan is under 12 inches. Crowded beans steam and go army green.
Trim the stem ends only. The wispy tails are perfectly good and take twice as long to remove.
This works just as well with sugar snap peas or broccolini — same heat, same hands-off start.
recipes.cooksNote: This is my go-to Thanksgiving vegetable because it needs no oven space and takes twelve minutes at the very end when everything else is resting. You can trim the beans and slice the garlic the morning before; just keep the garlic under a damp paper towel so it does not dry out and burn.

recipes.title: Salt and Vinegar Smashed Roast Potatoes
recipes.author: Recipe Mom
recipes.desc: Boiled in vinegar water, smashed flat, and roasted in hot fat until the edges shatter like a chip.
recipes.lede: Boiling potatoes in heavily vinegared water does two things at once: it seasons them right through, and the acid keeps them from collapsing while you get them fully soft. Then you smash them, which multiplies the surface area, and roast them in hot fat until every ragged edge goes glassy. They are the best potatoes I make and my family will not let me serve anything else.

items.name: duck fat or olive oil
items.note: duck fat if you have it

steps.title: Boil in vinegar water
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a large pot with the water, white vinegar and kosher salt, bring to a boil, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes. They are done when a knife slides into the center and out again with absolutely no resistance — undercooked potatoes will not smash, they will crumble.

steps.title: Drain and steam dry
steps.text: Drain well and leave the potatoes in the colander for 5 minutes. The surfaces should go from wet and shiny to matte and floury; that dry surface is what turns crisp in the oven.

steps.title: Heat the fat
steps.text: Meanwhile heat the oven to 450F (230C), pour the duck fat or oil onto a heavy sheet pan, and put the pan in the oven for 6 minutes until the fat is properly hot and beginning to ripple. Cold fat means the potatoes absorb it instead of frying in it.

steps.title: Smash
steps.text: Set the potatoes on the hot pan and press each one flat with the bottom of a glass or a spatula until it is about 1/2 inch thick and the edges have cracked apart. You want ragged, not neat — every crack is another crisp edge.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Tuck in the garlic and rosemary, season with the pepper, and roast 20 minutes. Flip each potato with a thin spatula and roast another 15 to 18 minutes, until both sides are deep golden brown and the thin edges look almost translucent and lift off the pan cleanly.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with the malt vinegar while they are still blazing hot so it hisses and vanishes into the surface, then flaky salt and chives. Serve straight away — these are at their best for about ten minutes and merely very good after that.

tips: Use a heavy metal sheet pan, never glass or a nonstick tray. You need the pan to hold real heat when the cold potatoes land on it.
Boil the potatoes up to a day ahead and refrigerate them uncovered. Chilled, dried-out potatoes crisp even better.
Do not crowd the pan. Two pans with room around each potato beats one pan of steamed, pale ones.
Discard the rosemary before serving if the sprigs have gone dark — they turn bitter past golden brown.
recipes.cooksNote: The vinegar in the boiling water does not carry through as a flavor at all, so do not fear it — its job is to firm up the pectin so the potatoes hold their shape through a long boil. The malt vinegar at the end is the part you actually taste, and that one is worth buying a bottle for.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Tuna Salad
recipes.desc: Oil-packed albacore with tomato, red onion, capers and parsley — ten minutes, no stove.
recipes.lede: This is the lunch I make when I want something that actually holds me together till dinner. The trick is good tuna packed in olive oil — that oil is the whole dressing — and letting it sit five minutes so the onion softens its bite. Pile it over greens, stuff it into an avocado, or pull it apart on toast.

items.name: wild albacore tuna in olive oil

steps.title: Flake the tuna
steps.text: Tip the tuna into a medium bowl along with its olive oil and break it into big, craggy flakes with a fork — you want texture, not paste.

steps.title: Fold in the vegetables
steps.text: Add the diced tomato, red onion, capers and parsley. Fold everything together gently so the tomato does not break down.

steps.title: Dress and season
steps.text: Pour over the red wine vinegar, season with the salt and pepper, and toss until glossy. Taste and adjust — it should be bright and a little punchy.

steps.title: Rest, then serve
steps.text: Let it sit for five minutes so the onion mellows and the flavours settle. Serve over arugula with chickpeas, avocado and a jammy egg, or spread on toasted sourdough.

tips: Buy the tuna packed in olive oil, not water — that oil is your dressing, so never drain it.
Five minutes of resting is not optional; it takes the raw edge off the onion and pulls everything together.
Doubles and triples cleanly for a batch of lunches — it actually tastes better on day two.
recipes.cooksNote: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to two days and only improves overnight. Bring it back to room temperature before serving so the olive oil loosens again.

recipes.title: High-Fiber Overnight Oats
recipes.desc: Oats, chia and avocado powder soaked overnight into a thick, green, genuinely filling jar.
recipes.lede: This is the one I stir together at night so breakfast is already done. The chia does all the work while you sleep — by morning it is thick enough to stand a spoon in, and it actually holds you until lunch instead of leaving you rummaging at ten. It goes an alarming shade of green from the avocado powder; do not let that put you off.

items.name: blueberries or strawberries, to top
items.note: optional — a small handful of blueberries, or 2 to 3 strawberries

steps.title: Combine the dry
steps.text: Tip the oats, chia seeds, avocado powder and the cinnamon and flaxseed if you are using them into a jar or container with a lid.

steps.title: Pour in the milk
steps.text: Add the milk, pouring it right over the dry ingredients so nothing stays stuck to the sides.

steps.title: Stir properly
steps.text: Stir until there are no dry pockets and no powder clinging to the bottom — chia clumps if you rush this, so go round the base of the jar a few times.

steps.title: Chill overnight
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 to 8 hours. The chia swells and the oats soften until the whole thing is thick and spoonable.

steps.title: Stir and top
steps.text: In the morning give it another stir to loosen it, then scatter over the berries. If it has set firmer than you like, slacken it with a splash more milk.

tips: Give it a second stir a few minutes after the first — that is when the chia starts to seize and any clumps are still easy to break up.
Build three or four jars at once on a Sunday; they keep happily for a couple of days and breakfast stops being a decision.
If you are hungry again before lunch, eat it alongside a boiled egg or a small pot of plain Greek yogurt for extra protein.
recipes.cooksNote: Designed to keep you full and your blood sugar steady through the morning — the oats bring beta-glucan, the chia and flaxseed bring omega-3, and the milk adds calcium and magnesium. Best eaten cold, straight from the fridge.

recipes.title: Garlic & Oyster Sauce Tempeh Stir-Fry
recipes.desc: Fried tempeh, snappy French beans and chickpeas in a quick garlic and oyster sauce glaze.
recipes.lede: Thirteen minutes, one pan, and the sort of dinner that makes you feel organised. The whole point is heat and speed — the beans should stay squeaky and bright, not go dull and soft, so everything gets cut and measured before the oil goes in. Tempeh and chickpeas together make it properly filling without any meat.

items.name: French beans, trimmed and cut diagonally
water
items.note: to loosen it into a sauce

steps.title: Aromatise the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for about a minute, until it turns golden and smells sweet — do not let it catch or it will go bitter.

steps.title: Flash-cook the beans
steps.text: Tip in the French beans and push the heat up to medium-high. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until they turn a vivid bright green and still squeak against the spoon.

steps.title: Add the pulses and protein
steps.text: Add the boiled chickpeas and the fried tempeh slices. Toss for a minute so everything is evenly spread through the pan and heated right through.

steps.title: Sauce and simmer
steps.text: Drizzle over the oyster sauce and soy sauce, then pour in the water. Stir-fry hard for 1 to 2 minutes, letting the liquid bubble up and coat everything — the beans should soften just slightly and stay crisp.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Take it off the heat straight away and turn it out onto a serving plate. It carries on cooking in a hot wok, so do not let it sit.

tips: Cut and measure everything before the pan gets hot. Eight minutes of cooking leaves no time to be trimming beans halfway through.
Frying the tempeh first is what gives it that firm, golden edge — straight from the packet it will steam and go soft in the sauce.
Oyster sauce is not vegetarian. Swap in a mushroom-based vegetarian oyster sauce and the dish becomes fully plant-based.
recipes.cooksNote: The beans are the thing to watch. Pull the pan off while they still have a squeak and a bright colour — a minute too long and they slump and grey out. A splash more water is fine if the sauce tightens before the beans are ready.
